Given the name, write the charge
Given the formula, write the charge

ions.name: ammonium
ions.explanation: Ammonium is NH₄⁺, the only common polyatomic cation in this set. Do not confuse it with ammonia (NH₃), which is a neutral molecule.

ions.name: nitrite
ions.explanation: Nitrite is NO₂⁻. The -ite ending means one fewer oxygen than the -ate ion nitrate (NO₃⁻). Both carry a 1− charge.

ions.name: nitrate
ions.explanation: Nitrate is NO₃⁻. Nitrite (NO₂⁻) has one fewer oxygen and the same 1− charge.

ions.name: sulfite
ions.explanation: Sulfite is SO₃²⁻. Sulfate (SO₄²⁻) has one more oxygen; both ions carry a 2− charge.

ions.name: sulfate
ions.explanation: Sulfate is SO₄²⁻. Sulfite is the related ion with one fewer oxygen (SO₃²⁻).

ions.name: hydroxide
ions.explanation: Hydroxide is OH⁻. Do not confuse it with oxide (O²⁻) or peroxide (O₂²⁻).

ions.name: cyanide
ions.explanation: Cyanide is CN⁻, a diatomic anion with a 1− charge.

ions.name: phosphate
ions.explanation: Phosphate is PO₄³⁻, one of the few common 3− polyatomic ions. Hydrogen phosphate (HPO₄²⁻) is a different ion.

ions.name: carbonate
ions.explanation: Carbonate is CO₃²⁻. Hydrogen carbonate / bicarbonate (HCO₃⁻) is related but has a 1− charge.

ions.name: hypochlorite
ions.explanation: Hypochlorite is ClO⁻, the lowest-oxygen member of the chlorine oxoanion series: hypo-…-ite, -ite, -ate, per-…-ate.

ions.name: chlorite
ions.explanation: Chlorite is ClO₂⁻. The chlorine series is ClO⁻ (hypochlorite), ClO₂⁻ (chlorite), ClO₃⁻ (chlorate), ClO₄⁻ (perchlorate).

ions.name: chlorate
ions.explanation: Chlorate is ClO₃⁻. Perchlorate (ClO₄⁻) has one more oxygen; chlorite (ClO₂⁻) has one fewer.

ions.name: perchlorate
ions.explanation: Perchlorate is ClO₄⁻, the highest-oxygen chlorine oxoanion. The per-…-ate prefix marks one more oxygen than the -ate ion.

ions.name: acetate
ions.explanation: Acetate is C₂H₃O₂⁻ (also written CH₃COO⁻). It is a 1− carboxylate anion, not a 2− ion.

ions.name: permanganate
ions.explanation: Permanganate is MnO₄⁻. Despite four oxygens, the charge is 1−, not 2−.

ions.name: dichromate
ions.explanation: Dichromate is Cr₂O₇²⁻. Chromate is CrO₄²⁻ — same 2− charge, different formula.

ions.name: chromate
ions.explanation: Chromate is CrO₄²⁻. Dichromate (Cr₂O₇²⁻) has the same charge but two chromium atoms.

ions.name: peroxide
ions.explanation: Peroxide is O₂²⁻ (two oxygens, 2− charge). Oxide is O²⁻; superoxide is O₂⁻.
